technical_and_design_decisions: Target platform is Spring XD (built on Spring Framework 6 / Spring Integration), with Java 17+.
Message bus abstraction is assumed to be pluggable (RabbitMQ as the primary target, Redis as a secondary case), with a clean provider interface used to add destroy/cleanup hooks.
U1 and U2 are implemented together as a unified 'stream-destroy cleanup' lifecycle that removes both actively-bound and stale queues/topics/exchanges for the destroyed stream's modules.
U3 is implemented as an in-place 'redeploy' flow that tears down only the bus bindings and redeploys modules with new properties, avoiding the need for a full destroy/create cycle.

U4 is implemented as a deployment-manifest loader that reads a properties/YAML file (in addition to the existing inline --properties), with merge semantics (file values act as defaults, inline values override).

U6 uses Spring Integration's global wiretap pattern, configured dynamically from the deployment properties (module.<name>.trace or module.*.trace) so the same code path supports single-module and wildcard tracing.
U7 reuses the wiretap mechanism from U6 plus a 'side channel' declaration on the stream DSL to create additional named channels beyond input/output, used for in-flow tap/tracking.
U5 is delivered as a set of curated reference architecture markdown docs plus minimal runnable POCs (no full enterprise-ready architectures).
U8 is implemented as a runnable Spring XD stream + simple analytics sink/aggregator reading the NYC taxi dataset from a public source, with documentation of how to run it.
Testing strategy: JUnit 5 unit tests for each module, plus integration tests using an embedded/test message bus (or a containerized broker) for stream lifecycle and tracing scenarios.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work; familiarity with Spring Integration, Spring XD, and AMQP/RabbitMQ is assumed.
The existing Spring XD codebase, build system (Gradle), and CI are already in place; no bootstrapping of repositories is required.
A test message broker (e.g., embedded Qpid or Dockerized RabbitMQ) is available for integration testing.
All estimates represent productive development effort, not calendar duration; no meetings, vacation, or onboarding are included.
No new external systems (e.g., a new datastore, a new message bus provider) are introduced beyond what Spring XD already supports.
The NYC taxi dataset is publicly downloadable; no special data acquisition or licensing work is required for U8.
Reference architectures (U5) are scoped as 'first-step' design captures, not production-ready reference implementations.
No migration of existing user data or streams is required; new behaviors are opt-in via deployment properties/CLI flags.

activities.activity_description: Review the existing Spring XD stream lifecycle, deployment, and message bus code paths; produce a technical design that covers the destroy/cleanup hooks, in-place redeploy, manifest loader, tracing/wiretap, and side-channel mechanisms; align with the eight user stories.

activities.activity_name: Implement stream-destroy cleanup of message bus resources (U1 + U2)
activities.activity_description: Add a destroy-time cleanup hook to the stream lifecycle that deletes queues, topics, and exchanges associated with the stream's modules, including stale resources from prior failed destroys.

activities.activity_name: Implement edit/redeploy of a deployed stream (U3)
activities.activity_description: Extend the deploy command/flow to support updating the deployment properties of an already-deployed stream by undeploying and redeploying in place, without requiring destroy + recreate of the stream definition.

activities.activity_name: Implement deployment manifest loaded from a file (U4)
activities.activity_description: Add support for the deploy command to read deployment properties from a file path (in addition to inline --properties), with a clear merge/override policy between file and inline values.

activities.activity_name: Implement inline trace deployment properties via wiretap (U6)
activities.activity_description: Parse module.<name>.trace and module.*.trace from deployment properties and apply the Spring Integration global wiretap to the targeted modules' channels so messages are intercepted for logging/notification.

activities.activity_name: Implement arbitrary side channels in a stream flow (U7)
activities.activity_description: Extend the stream DSL/module model to allow declaring additional named channels beyond input/output, create the corresponding bus resources, and expose them so a wiretap/tap can be used to track module progress.

activities.activity_name: Author Spring XD reference architecture documentation (U5)
activities.activity_description: Capture domain-specific reference architectures as design docs and small runnable POCs (e.g., real-time analytics, ETL, event-driven microservices) for field engineers to use as starting points.

activities.activity_name: Build NYC taxi trips demo/evaluation application (U8)
activities.activity_description: Implement a runnable Spring XD stream that ingests the DEBS 2015 NYC taxi trip reports, performs simple real-time analytics, and documents how to run and evaluate it.
Write JUnit 5 unit tests for the new lifecycle hooks, redeploy flow, manifest loader, wiretap property parsing, side-channel creation, and reference-architecture POC building blocks.

Write end-to-end integration tests against an embedded/test message broker covering: destroy cleanup of queues/topics, in-place redeploy with new properties, manifest-from-file deployment, trace/wiretap message capture, side-channel tap, and the taxi demo stream.

Update the Spring XD reference documentation with new CLI flags, deployment property formats, side-channel DSL syntax, reference architecture index, and the taxi demo runbook; add release notes summarizing the increment.
